h1: Becoming a wine sommelier in India: training and first jobs
title: Becoming a Wine Sommelier in India | Craft Beer School
desc: How to train as a wine sommelier in India: the certifications, the skills employers test and where first jobs actually come from.
teaser: Sommeliers are made on the restaurant floor as much as in the classroom. Here is the honest route in.
standfirst: A sommelier in India sells wine to guests who often know little about it, in heat that punishes careless storage. This guide covers the training, the skills that matter and the jobs where most careers start.
sections:
Most people picture a sommelier swirling a glass and reciting tasting notes. The real job is closer to running a small, perishable stock business inside a restaurant. A sommelier buys wine, stores it properly, builds the list, prices it, trains the floor staff and then sells it to guests one table at a time.

In India the job has an extra layer. Many guests are ordering wine for the first time, or they are beer and whisky drinkers trying something new. A good sommelier here is a translator first. They find out what the guest likes to eat and drink, then pick a bottle that fits the food and the budget without making anyone feel foolish.

Two families of qualification carry weight with Indian hotels and importers.

  • WSET (Wine and Spirit Education Trust). Levels 1 to 3 in wines, then the Level 4 Diploma. WSET is about knowledge: regions, grapes, winemaking and a structured way of tasting. Courses run through approved providers in several Indian cities and online.
  • Court of Master Sommeliers. Introductory, Certified, Advanced and Master levels. The Court tests service as well as theory: opening and pouring at the table, decanting and blind tasting under time pressure.

WSET Level 2 is a sensible first target for a career changer. It gives you enough vocabulary to talk to guests and suppliers. Level 3 is where employers start to take you seriously for a wine-focused role. We compare these and other drinks qualifications in our certifications guide.
The skills nobody prints on the certificate

A certificate gets you an interview. These get you the job and keep it.

  • Tasting with discipline. Being able to say a wine is corked, oxidised or cooked by heat before a guest sends it back. Our guide to wine tasting for beginners is a fair place to start practising.
  • Food knowledge. Indian menus are spicy, layered and often served all at once. Knowing why an off-dry white survives a Chettinad curry when a big oaky red does not is worth more than memorising Burgundy villages.
  • Cellar arithmetic. Cost price, menu price, stock days and wastage on wines poured by the glass.
  • Service under pressure. Opening a bottle cleanly at a crowded table while answering a question about the vintage.

Responsible tasting is part of the job. Professionals taste and spit through long sessions. A good sommelier never pushes a guest to order more than they want.

Very few people start with the title. The usual routes in are:

  • Restaurant or bar service in a five-star hotel, moving into the wine team once you show interest and knowledge.
  • Sales roles at wine importers and distributors, which supply hotels, clubs and premium retail.
  • Tasting room and hospitality roles at Indian wineries in Nashik, Karnataka and elsewhere.
  • Premium liquor retail in states that allow walk-in browsing stores.
  • Cruise lines and hotels abroad, which many Indian hospitality graduates use to build experience.

A hotel management background helps but is not required. People also arrive from beer and spirits, which is a natural move. Our guide to a beer sommelier career shows how much the two paths overlap.

This is where many aspiring sommeliers stall. They can name a grape but cannot explain why a Nashik Sauvignon Blanc tastes different from a New Zealand one. They do not know why a wine has gone flat in a hotel storeroom at 32 °C. Guests and employers ask exactly these questions.

Knowing how wine is made answers most of them. Once you understand fermentation, sulphur dioxide, malolactic conversion, oak and closures, a wine list stops being a list of names. It becomes a set of decisions somebody made, which you can explain to a guest in one sentence.

1. Get a front-of-house job where wine is sold, even if wine is not your role yet.
  2. Complete WSET Level 2 within the first few months.
  3. Learn how wine is made, so you can explain style and faults from the cause rather than from memory.
  4. Taste with a group every week, blind where you can. Keep written notes.
  5. Ask to help with stock counts and the wine list. That is where the commercial side of the job is learnt.

None of this needs a large budget. It needs regular practice and people around you who will correct you.
faqs: Do I need a hotel management degree to become a sommelier in India?
No. It helps with hotel jobs, but importers, wineries and restaurants also hire people from other backgrounds who can show knowledge, tasting skill and good service.
Which certification should I start with?
WSET Level 2 in Wines is a practical first step for most career changers. If you are aiming at fine dining service, the Court of Master Sommeliers Introductory course is worth adding later.
Do sommeliers have to drink a lot?
No. Professionals taste and spit, often across dozens of wines in a session. Staying clear-headed is part of the job.
